findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-DADDEZIO-23.result.json item 19, route 4 and route 6 application item 68; GlobalShtukasPartIICrystallineCompanions
findings.claim: The consumer promises the isocrystal attached to every cuspidal representation but imports a finite-central-character theorem with no twisting adapter. Route 4 says that it consumes Abe exactly as the accepted brief states it and adds no target; the accepted supplier has the extra finite-order hypothesis.
findings.evidence: PAPER-ABE-18/32 and accepted route 2 restrict the central character to finite order. Abe, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1310.0528v3, Theorem 4.2.2 p.103, defines A_r by “the order of the central character of π is finite”. DAD route 4 instead says “every” representation and “It adds no target”. Rank one a↦c^deg(a), c of infinite order, is an explicit input excluded from A_r. DAD v4 proof of Theorem 5.3.3 p.27 is the consumer. The accepted Abe brief and structured related routes do not supply the automorphic twisting compatibility.
findings.fix: Keep Abe’s precise finite-order theorem and the general DAD application. Add the reduction by an unramified degree character at GlobalShtukasPartIICrystallineCompanions, reusing function-field class field theory: normalize the central character, apply Abe, and untwist by the matching constant rank-one isocrystal. Prove the Frobenius/Hecke convention and slope-shift compatibility; test an infinite-order rank-one degree character. Remove the inaccurate adds-no-target assertion. Do not build a second correspondence or silently restrict item 68.

findings.claim: Item 1 marks an entire mixed bundle planned at RD.3 although it includes an unassigned F-infinity 2-colimit construction and crystalline comparison. Its own note acknowledges the mismatch. No route includes item 1, while the later Lambda and exact-sequence constructions require its carrier and transition coherence.
findings.evidence: The item-1 note says the crystalline description/comparison is not named at RD.3 and the 2-colimit is “this paper’s construction”. The complete RD.3 contract builds frames, coefficient descent, Frobenius structures and restriction, not the divisibility-indexed transition category. Route accounting finds item 1 outside every route. DAD v4 §2.2 p.6 defines the additional carrier; its displayed iteration has F* where (F^n)* is needed for n>1, verified in the page image.
findings.fix: Split covered foundations from missing additions. Route the crystalline comparison to the RD.3 owner with the CR.3 input. Assign the F-infinity construction to an early route-6 layer preceding Lambda: positive integers ordered by divisibility, Frobenius-power transitions, coherence, eventual morphisms, exact tensor structure and scalar conventions. Use a correctly typed (F^n)* iteration and record the localized v4 misprint if adding sourceIssues. Test n=2,m=2 and n→nm→nml. Preserve parent ownership of ordinary coefficient categories.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-DADDEZIO-23.result.json items 33/35/42/50 and route 6 layer (2), base change and intersection formulas
findings.claim: The group attached to the specified Omega-valued fibre functor is over K(Omega), but items 42 and 50 extend the Q_p^ur group only to K=K(k). The first resulting group isomorphism is false as an isomorphism over K(k) for general Omega/k; the intersection does not specify two subgroups over the same ambient field.
findings.evidence: DAD v4 §2.2 p.6 defines omega_eta with values in Vec_K(Omega); §3.1 p.7 fixes K:=K(k), and Definition 3.1.2 extends the lattice to K(Omega). Proposition 3.3.2 p.10 and Corollary 4.3.6 p.19 nevertheless print extension to K; all four page images were checked. Items 42/50 and route 6 copy this without a descended-form convention. For k=F_p^alg, Omega=algebraic_closure(k(t)), X=Spec k and the unit coefficient, the two trivial group schemes have coordinate rings K(Omega) and K(k); a K(k)-algebra isomorphism between these cannot exist. Existing E2 fixes a dual-fibre formula only.
findings.fix: Keep K(k) in the category scalar-extension equivalence. For the monodromy group of omega_eta, extend to K(Omega) and supply the compatible fibre-functor identification. Put both intersection factors in GL(omega_eta M) over K(Omega). Alternatively name the descended K(k)-form separately and explicitly base-change it. Propagate through the exact-square and intersection API, add the strict-extension unit test, and record the source issue only for the inspected v4. Do not reject the categorical equivalence or parabolicity theorem.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-DADDEZIO-23.result.json item 33 and route 6, compared with accepted PAPER-ABE-18/25 route 1, PadicDifferentialEquationsPartIIArithmeticDModules
findings.claim: Route 6 gives a new basic Crew construction and asserts that no proposal plans it, but accepted Abe item 25 already assigns the overconvergent fundamental/Weil-group construction to arithmetic D-modules. The shared coefficient-extended overconvergent scope has no common owner or comparison contract. This finding does not identify every DAD group or theorem with Abe’s scope.
findings.evidence: DAD route 6 says “No layer or proposal plans Crew’s monodromy groups”. PAPER-ABE-18/25 explicitly calls its input “Crew’s monodromy groups in the Weil-group form Lafforgue uses”; accepted route 1 includes that item and Weil groups in its brief. Abe v3 §2.4.17 pp.86–87 constructs Aut-tensor of the overconvergent fibre category; restricting to the object-generated tensor subcategory gives the object monodromy quotient. Abe uses algebraically extended coefficients; DAD uses K(Omega). A common-field comparison is needed, not literal equality of differently typed groups.
findings.fix: Coordinate route 6 with the existing arithmetic-D-module owner through an early shared Crew prefix. Reuse its construction on the overlap and prove coefficient/fibre comparison and object-generated quotient compatibility. Retain the extra convergent, perfect-point, punctual Q_p^ur and parabolicity work in DAD. Correct the no-prior-owner assertion and the Bessel consumer instruction. Keep generic reconstruction at MC.6. Do not make the whole arithmetic-D-module roadmap depend on the whole DAD monodromy roadmap: D-modules→Abe→DAD applications must remain downstream of the common prefix.
